Meta.title: System Design Interview Roadmap
Meta.description: A bilingual, open-source roadmap for studying system design with a focus on interviews.

Home.title: Master <hl>system design</hl> one building block at a time.
Home.subtitle: A guided, developer-first roadmap that turns scattered system design theory into a clear path — from DNS and load balancers to full interview walkthroughs. Built from real course notes and kept as a public, living study log.
Home.schemaCaption: Every topic is typed, validated content — so the roadmap builds itself.
Home.introTitle: A guided path, not a pile of open tabs.
Home.introLead: System design is broad, and most resources throw you straight into the deep end. This repository breaks it into small, ordered building blocks you can actually finish — each explained the same way, in English and Portuguese.
Home.whatBody: An open-source study log for system design interviews: fundamental building blocks, interview topics, and practical end-to-end examples — structured as focused topic pages.
Home.whoBody: Beginner and entry-level developers preparing for their first system design interviews — and anyone who learns better from a roadmap than from a stack of disconnected articles.
Home.howBody: It grows lesson by lesson. After each class, new notes become a topic — with key concepts, trade-offs, interview relevance, and a beginner summary, in both languages.
Home.roadmapSubtitle: Follow the path from the fundamentals to full interview walkthroughs. Every node is a topic page — click any to dive in.
Home.ctaBody: Open the roadmap and follow it top to bottom, or jump straight to the building block you need.
Home.emptyStage: Coming soon — content for this section is on the way.
